newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set fresh record with 1.12 pct rise.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set fresh record with 1.12 pct rise.

text.p: French shares closed at a fresh record high after a 1.2 percent jump on Thursday, underpinned by a rising dollar and further gains on Wall Street.

The market shrugged off January U.S. retail sales, which were broadly in line with expectations, and lower weekly jobless claims. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan is due to speak later on Thursday.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 29.08 points or 1.12 percent at 2,628.41, after hitting an intra-day high of 2,631.89, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 30 points at 2,635. Volume was 10.4 billion francs.

Bouygues dropped 5.15 percent to 553 francs and Generale des Eaux set an all-time high of 802 francs after railraod company SNCF selected Generale and not Bouygues to become the operator of its nation-wide optic fibre network.

Lagardere was unchanged at 164.50 francs. The company confirmed its had lodged an appeal against a Privatisation Commission decision which led to the suspension of a deal under which Lagardere and Daewoo Electronics would have bought Thomson SA from the state.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe reiterated on Thursday he would announce a decision on the sale of Thomson-CSF before end-Feb.
Juppe met Thomson chairman Marcel Roulet, Lagardere head Jean-Luc Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk on Thursday to discuss the matter.
Alcatel was down 2.05 percent at 573 francs as five percent stake owner ITT is seeking permission to sell shares before the July expiration of a shareholders pact.
